`password-protected.pdf` contains the three original pages generated by
`tests/pdf_fixture.py`. The fixture content is CC0-1.0; it contains no user book
or credentials. It was encrypted offline with pypdf 6.18.1 using the standard
PDF RC4-128 test mode and fixed public passwords:

- User password: `reader-fixture`
- Owner password: `reader-fixture-owner`

This exercises the real Poppler password-required error during an OPDS HTTP
download. The GTK smoke test also opens the same file directly in Poppler with
the public test password, proving that it is a valid three-page encrypted PDF.
Reader itself does not unlock password-protected books.

The weak legacy cipher is used only for a compatibility test with public text,
not for protecting data. pypdf is an offline fixture authoring tool and is not
a Reader runtime or test-run dependency.
